title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for parallel multi-tool calls, result injection and retries
author: Jae Park
description:
Motivation: Multiple customers and internal evals surfaced fragility when (1) a single user request triggers multiple tool calls in parallel, (2) tool outputs need to be re-injected into the ongoing model generation, and (3) transient tool failures require deterministic retry behavior. This PR consolidates several ergonomics improvements to the tool-calling execution pipeline: clearer APIs for multi-tool parallel invocation, deterministic result injection ordering options, explicit retry policies with idempotency hints, and safer streaming boundaries to avoid partial output corruption.

Summary of changes: high-level commits (see commits list) implement: - a new ParallelToolExecutor abstraction that coordinates launching, cancelation, and backpressure for N parallel tool calls, with per-tool timeouts and cooperative cancellation hooks; - result-injection middleware that supports three injection modes (serial-ordered, best-effort-async, merge-by-key) so downstream prompts can be deterministically reconstructed; - retry policy DSL (max_attempts, backoff_ms, retry_on = [503, timeout, transient]) and idempotency tokens plumbed from the API layer to tool adapters; - streaming guard rails to ensure tool result boundaries are emitted as atomic blocks in the response stream, avoiding partial JSON/structured outputs; - OpenAI-compat layer updates to keep response shape compatible while enabling the new injection modes via beta flags; - tests, docs, and migration notes.

Compatibility and rollout: default behavior is backwards-compatible: existing tool-calling flows map to the serial-ordered injection and conservative retry policy (max_attempts=1). New behavior is behind an opt-in feature flag and SDK/compat shim will expose helpers in Python/TS SDKs. The change is gated by an internal rollout (canary on ~5% of traffic, then 25%, 100%) and includes metrics/alerts for injection failures and retry rates.

Reasoning and trade-offs: Parallel execution reduces tail latency but increases complexity around prompt reconstruction and hallucination risk if tool outputs arrive out-of-order. We chose to provide explicit injection modes so caller libraries and server-side policies can pick the right consistency/latency trade-off. Retries are explicit and require idempotency from tool adapters; conservative defaults avoid double-side effects by default.

Testing and validation: unit tests for executor cancellation and ordering, integration tests against mock tool backends that simulate latency spikes and transient HTTP 5xx errors, end-to-end QA with streaming clients to validate structured output boundaries, load test showing 18% median latency improvement for a 3-tool parallel workload under mixed tail latencies.

Notes: See release_notes for user-facing guidance; migration steps included in docs and SDK PRs.

review_comments: Ava Chen (2026-02-16): Can you clarify behavior when one tool permanently fails but others succeed? Is the overall response partial or does it fail the request?

Jae Park (2026-02-16): By default we return partial response with an error block for the failed tool and include retry metadata. Teams can opt into strict-failure mode via request param; note documented trade-offs.
Marcus Li (2026-02-17): Suggest renaming merge-by-key to keyed-merge for clarity and align SDK helpers. Also add a metric for out-of-order injections.
Jae Park (2026-02-17): Renamed to keyed-merge and added reorder metrics. Updated tests to assert metric emission.
Priya Nair (2026-02-18): Approve after small nits on wording in docs. Verified canary telemetry looks good.
Liam O'Connor (2026-02-19): Approve. Confirmed OpenAI-compat header remains backwards compatible when omitted.
release_notes: Tool-calling: added ParallelToolExecutor, configurable result injection modes (serial-ordered, best-effort-async, keyed-merge), explicit retry policy DSL with idempotency support, and streaming guardrails to ensure atomic tool-result frames. Backwards-compatible by default; new behaviors behind opt-in beta flag. See docs/tool-calling/parallel-exec.md for migration steps.
migration_notes: Default behavior unchanged: existing tool calls continue to be injected serially and have max_attempts=1. To opt in, pass injection_mode and retry_policy in the call options. SDKs expose helpers: Python: ToolCallOptions(injection_mode='keyed-merge', retry_policy=RetryPolicy(...)); TS equivalent in SDK. Canary rollout plan described in docs.
perf_impact_summary: Parallel execution enabled ~18% median latency improvement for 3-tool workflows under mixed tail conditions; 5-15% higher p95 depending on backend variance. Additional CPU/memory used for executor coordination is small (<3%).
testing_summary: Unit tests for executor lifecycle, retry policies and middleware; integration tests against mock tool backends simulating 5xx and timeouts; e2e streaming test ensures atomic frames and structured output intact; load tests used to validate canary rollout.
notes: Follow-up work: (1) expose server-side throttling heuristics for heavy parallel workloads, (2) add operator-visible signals for idempotency violations, (3) SDK ergonomics for automatic idempotency token generation.
